clauses.clause: This spell costs {3} less to cast if you've gained 3 or more life this turn.
clauses.evidence: [cast targets=['you_fallen']] pays the full {3}{B} (mana B-1 W-3) with no life gained. Tree abilities[0] equals the compiler's B4-cost-modifier-conditional-life parse. Covered by packs: sanguine_indulgence_reduced_two_targets.json (you gain 3 via lifelink, cast spends only {B} of four B) PASS; sanguine_indulgence_not_reduced.json (you gain 2, the opponent gains 3: full {3}{B} paid) PASS.

clauses.clause: Return up to two target creature cards from your graveyard to your hand.
clauses.evidence: target slot (cast): 1..1 of [you_fallen] (your graveyard creature cards only: you_used and opp_fallen not offered); [cast targets=['you_fallen']]: 'you_fallen moves graveyard -> hand'. The two-target case is covered by pack sanguine_indulgence_reduced_two_targets.json (two of three graveyard creatures targeted: exactly those two return, the third, a noncreature and the opponent's creature card stay) PASS.
clauses.issue: Engine convention, not a tree fault: an 'up to N' TARGET slot is declared 1..N (MTG_bot/core/executor/query.py C17 comment), so the spell cannot be cast choosing zero targets, which the printed 'up to two' allows (CR 601.2c). This only makes the card weaker, never stronger.
